subject: arts-music
unit_title: Portfolio, Artist Statement, and Critical Review
essential_question: How does revision, rather than production, make a portfolio cohere?
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Presenting
project_brief: Curate a sophomore portfolio with revision evidence, a refined statement, and a completed rights and permissions audit. This is the grade 10 culminating project for "Portfolio, Artist Statement, and Critical Review" (ma-g10-arts-and-music-u06, unit 6), built around portfolio curation and cohesion, revision from critique evidence, artist statement refinement, documentation standards, and rights and permissions audit. Curate a sophomore portfolio with revision evidence, a refined statement, and a completed rights and permissions audit. Ground every claim in something specific you can point to in the work itself or in its documented historical/cultural context, covering portfolio curation and cohesion, revision from critique evidence, artist statement refinement, and documentation standards.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: portfolio curation and cohesion, revision from critique evidence, artist statement refinement, documentation standards, rights and permissions audit, and presentation and feedback cycle.
Meet the performance task as written: Curate a sophomore portfolio with revision evidence, a refined statement, and a completed rights and permissions audit.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Curate a sophomore portfolio with revision evidence, a refined statement, and a completed rights and permissions audit. Ground every claim in something specific you can point to in the work itself or in its documented historical/cultural context, covering portfolio curation and cohesion, revision from critique evidence, artist statement refinement, and documentation standards.
critique_criteria: A named viewer, listener, or reader can point to a specific choice in the work and connect it back to portfolio curation and cohesion or another named topic from this unit.
The piece shows at least one deliberate revision — a version-two decision made because the first attempt did not achieve the intended effect.
The student can explain the intended effect on an audience in their own words, separate from just describing what was made.
Only the student's own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt appears in the piece — no unlicensed lyrics, sheet music, or protected work is reproduced.
Every interpretive claim about the work is backed by a specific, quoted or cited piece of evidence from the work or its context, not a general impression.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: Sharing this project publicly is always optional and never required for full credit. You may present live to a small audience of your choosing, present privately to just your facilitator, submit a recording made only for your own review, or submit a written/described account of the finished work instead.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: If any part of this task could involve singing, speaking on camera, or being recorded, you may instead notate the piece, write a detailed description or script, use body percussion or an instrument in place of your voice, or perform live for your facilitator with no recording made at all. No lesson in this unit requires a voice recording, a camera, or a photo.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Use only your own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt — never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or another protected work without the rights to do so.
remediation: If the piece isn't coming together, return to a single, smaller exercise focused only on portfolio curation and cohesion, revisit one worked example or model from this unit, and rebuild your confidence with that one element before returning to the full project.
extension: Once the core piece is finished, create a second short variation that explores revision from critique evidence from a different angle, or write a short artist's statement comparing your original intent with what the finished work actually communicates.
